q: 1. The total discharge from two wells situated near to each other is .............
options: sum of the discharges from individual wells
greater than the sum of the discharges from the wells
less than the sum of the discharges from the wells
explain: Interference between the drawdown cones of nearby wells reduces the effective hydraulic gradient, so combined discharge is less than the simple sum of individual well discharges.

q: 2. Passive earth pressure is defined as
options: retaining wall tends to move away from the back fill
retaining wall tends to move towards the back fill
retaining wall is in stationary position
explain: Passive pressure develops when the wall is pushed into (moves towards) the backfill, compressing the soil to mobilize maximum resistance.

q: 3. When the steady seepage occurs in an isotropic soil, the head causing the flow satisfies the following equation .............
explain: Steady seepage through an isotropic, homogeneous soil is governed by Laplace's equation, the basis for flow net construction.

q: 4. Total lateral earth pressure is proportional to
options: angle of internal friction of soil
explain: Total pressure (force) on a wall = ½·K·γ·H² (area under the triangular pressure diagram), making total earth pressure proportional to the square of the retained depth H.

q: 5. Earth pressure at rest can be defined as lateral pressure exerted by the soil when the retaining wall tends to
options: no movement relative to the backfill
explain: At-rest earth pressure occurs when the wall is rigid and does not move at all relative to the backfill (zero lateral strain condition).

q: 6. In order to increase the FS against piping .............
options: a blanket of impermeable material is laid for same length along the downstream ground surface
pump out the water periodically, downstream
explain: Placing an impervious blanket downstream lengthens the seepage path and increases the weight resisting uplift, raising the factor of safety against piping.

q: 7. The base width of retaining wall is B. What is the maximum, permissible eccentricity if the wall should not fail in tension?
explain: To avoid tension at the base (keeping the resultant within the middle third), the eccentricity must not exceed B/6, per the middle-third rule for rectangular sections.

q: 8. A coarse grained soil has a void ratio of 0.7 and specific gravity of 2.7. The critical gradient at which the quick sand condition occurs is .............
9. Earth pressure acting at a height of ........ in case of inclined surcharge
options: h/2 from the base of the wall
h/3 from the base of the wall
h/4 from the base of the wall
h/5 from the base of the wall
explain: For a wall with inclined surcharge, the resultant earth pressure (trapezoidal-type distribution due to surcharge) acts at approximately h/4 above the base, as per standard design charts.

q: 10. The seepage flow through a porous medium is generally .............
explain: Seepage velocities in soils are typically low enough (low Reynolds number) that flow is laminar, satisfying Darcy's law.

q: 11. The assumption of Rankine's theory of earth pressure is
options: the soil is semi finite, homogeneous, dry and cohesionless
ground surface is a plane which may be inclined or horizontal
back of the wall is vertical and smooth
explain: Rankine's theory assumes a semi-infinite, homogeneous, cohesionless, dry soil mass, a planar ground surface, and a vertical, smooth wall back — all these assumptions together define the theory.

q: 12. Criterion for the design of an inverted filter is .............
options: D15 of filter/D85 of base < 5 < D15 of filter/D15 of base
D15 of base/D15 of filter < 5 < D15 of base/D15 of base
D15 of filter/D15 of base < 5 < D85 of filter/D85 of base
D15 of base/D85 of base < 5 < D85 of base/D85 of base
explain: The inverted filter design criterion ensures the filter is permeable enough (via D15/D85 ratio) yet fine enough to retain base soil particles.

q: 13. In the case of retaining walls, surcharge is
options: additional load carrying capacity of wall
extra load on the horizontal backfill
explain: Surcharge refers to any additional load (e.g., traffic, stacked material) placed on the horizontal backfill surface behind a retaining wall, which increases lateral pressure.

q: 14. The bearing capacity of soil
options: depends on the size of the footing
explain: Bearing capacity theories (e.g., Terzaghi's) show the ultimate bearing capacity depends on footing size/width (through the Nγ term), among other footing and soil parameters.

q: 15. The most suitable method for increasing the bearing capacity of black cotton soil is
options: replacement of black cotton soil by sand
explain: Because black cotton soil swells/shrinks excessively and has low bearing capacity, the most effective remedy is to replace it with a sand cushion/pad beneath the foundation.

q: 16. Bearing capacity of soil is determined by
options: both a. and b. of above
explain: Both the plate load test and standard (cone) penetration test are recognized field methods for estimating bearing capacity of soil.

q: 17. The soil having minimum/least bearing capacity is
explain: Moist (saturated) clay has very low shear strength and high compressibility, giving it the least bearing capacity among the listed soil types.

q: 18. A grillage foundation is used under
explain: Grillage foundations use layers of steel beams to spread heavy column loads over a large area economically, typically under a single heavily loaded isolated column.

q: 19. Who is known as the Father of 'Soil Mechanics'?
explain: Karl Terzaghi is universally credited as the 'Father of Soil Mechanics' for founding the discipline with his effective stress principle and consolidation theory.

q: 20. When a static load is applied, the consolidation is fast the case of .............
explain: Sands have high permeability, allowing pore water to drain and consolidation to occur almost instantaneously compared to fine-grained soils.

q: 21. Direct measurement of permeability of the soil specimen can be made at any stage of loading in .............
explain: In a fixed ring consolidometer, the sample geometry relative to the ring is known at all times, allowing direct permeability measurement at any load stage.

q: 22. If h is the head of water stored, Nf is the number of flow lines and Nd is the number of equipotential drops in a flow net, then the seepage flow rate is given by
explain: The standard flow-net discharge formula is q = k·h·(Nf/Nd), where Nf/Nd is the shape factor of the flow net.

q: 23. The consolidation settlement of a soil is
options: directly proportional to the voids ratio
explain: Consolidation settlement Sc = (Cc·H)/(1+e0)·log10[(σ0+Δσ)/σ0] is directly proportional to the compression index Cc.

q: 24. The strength theory applicable to a C-φ soil is
explain: A c-φ (cohesive-frictional) soil's shear strength is described by the Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion, s = c + σ·tanφ.

q: 25. Effective stress is
options: the stress at the particles contact
governing factor for the engineering properties
explain: Effective stress (Terzaghi's principle) is transmitted through particle-to-particle contacts, governs shear strength and compressibility, and is a real, measurable physical parameter — hence all statements are valid.

q: 26. In Mohr's stress circle, the co-ordinates of the center of the circle are
explain: Mohr's circle has its centre on the normal-stress axis at the average of major and minor principal stresses, i.e., ((σ1+σ3)/2, 0).

q: 27. In a flownet, which of the following statement is true?
options: Flow lines and equipotential lines intersect at oblique angles
Flow lines and equipotential lines intersect orthogonally
Flow rate through each flow channel is different
The head along each flow line is constant
explain: By construction, flow lines and equipotential lines in a properly drawn flow net always intersect at right angles (orthogonally).

q: 28. Shear strength of soil is determined by the equation
explain: Coulomb's shear strength equation is s = c + σ·tanφ, where s is shear strength, c is cohesion, σ is normal stress, and φ is the friction angle.

q: 29. The permeability of a soil deposit-in-situ can be best obtained by .............
explain: A field pumping test captures the actual in-situ permeability of a soil deposit, accounting for natural heterogeneity that lab tests cannot.

q: 30. The value of net allowable bearing pressure is
options: minimum of net safe bearing capacity and net safe settlement pressure
explain: Net allowable bearing pressure is taken as the smaller (governing) value between the pressure limited by shear failure (net safe bearing capacity) and that limited by tolerable settlement.

q: 31. The minimum number of observation wells required to determine the permeability of stratum in the field by pumping test is .............
explain: At least two observation wells at different radial distances are needed to establish the drawdown curve and calculate permeability.

q: 32. The Terzaghi's bearing capacity factors are functions of
options: friction angle between footing and soil
explain: Terzaghi's bearing capacity factors Nc, Nq, Nγ are all derived as functions solely of the soil's angle of internal friction φ.

q: 33. Over-consolidation may be due to .............
options: the weight of ice sheet or glacier which is melted away
weight of the land side which is removed
explain: Over-consolidation results from removal of a previously applied overburden, whether from a melted glacier or an eroded/removed landmass — both mechanisms apply.

q: 34. Even after the complete dissipation of excess pore pressure, a little more consolidation is possible. This is called as .............
explain: Secondary consolidation is the slow, creep-like compression that continues after primary consolidation (pore pressure dissipation) is complete.

q: 35. The coefficient of electro-osmotic permeability .............
options: is the same as the coefficient of hydraulic permeability
varies in the value over a wide range depending on the size of voids in the soil
varies in value over a wide range depending on the grain size of the sample
is almost independent of the grain size of the soil sample
explain: Unlike hydraulic permeability, electro-osmotic permeability depends mainly on the soil's zeta potential and double-layer properties, staying roughly independent of grain size.

q: 36. Bleeder wells are required to .............
explain: Bleeder wells relieve excess pore water pressure trapped beneath impervious layers, preventing uplift or blowout.

q: 37. Neutral stress refers to .............
explain: Neutral stress is another term for pore water pressure, the stress carried by water in the soil voids.

q: 38. The difference between total pressure and pore water pressure is known as .............
explain: Effective stress = total stress - pore water pressure, per Terzaghi's principle of effective stress.

q: 39. A flownet may be used for the determination of .............
explain: A flow net simultaneously provides exit gradient, seepage discharge, and seepage/uplift pressure at any point.

q: 40. Assumption in the Darcy' law is
explain: Darcy's law assumes an isotropic, homogeneous, incompressible, saturated soil with laminar (not turbulent) flow conditions.

q: 41. The angle of internal friction depends upon
explain: Friction angle is influenced by particle shape/roughness, degree of interlocking (density/angularity), and the normal stress level — all these factors jointly affect φ.

q: 42. Taylor's stability number is equal to Sn = c/(PHc) = c/(PH×FOS). For Hc, FOS=1
explain: When FOS = 1 (i.e., the critical/failure condition), the stability number simplifies to Sn = c/Hc, using the critical height Hc directly.

q: 43. According to ISS the minimum depths of foundation in sand and clay should be respectively
explain: As per Indian Standard code recommendations, minimum foundation depth in sand and clay generally falls in the range of about 80 cm to 90 cm, considering seasonal moisture variation and frost/shrinkage effects.

q: 44. Darcy's law is applicable if a soil is .............
explain: Darcy's law assumptions require the soil to be homogeneous, incompressible, and isotropic for validity of the linear flow relation.

q: 45. The maximum differential settlement is isolated footings on clayey soils should be limited to
explain: As per IS code guidance for isolated footings on clayey soils, the permissible differential settlement is typically limited to about 40 mm to avoid structural distress.

q: 46. According to Darcy's law, the flow velocity can be obtained by .............
explain: Darcy's law states discharge velocity v = Ki (permeability times hydraulic gradient).

q: 47. A combined footing is generally used when
options: Number of columns is more than two and they are spaced far apart
Number of columns is two and they are spaced far close to each other
Number of columns is two and they are spaced far apart
explain: A combined footing is provided when two columns are close enough that their individual isolated footings would overlap, so a single combined footing supports both.

q: 48. Coefficient of percolation has a value .............
options: less than the coefficient of permeability
equal to the coefficient of permeability
explain: Percolation velocity uses the effective (void) area rather than the gross area, making the coefficient of percolation greater than the coefficient of permeability.

q: 49. A plate load test is useful to estimate
options: Both bearing capacity and settlement of foundation
explain: The plate load test provides a load-settlement curve from which both the safe bearing capacity and the expected settlement of the actual foundation can be estimated.

q: 50. A shallow foundation is defined as a foundation which
options: Has a depth of embedment less than its width
Is resting on the ground surface
explain: By Terzaghi's definition, a foundation is 'shallow' when its depth of embedment (Df) is less than or approximately equal to its width (B), typically Df ≤ B.
